title: decoupled-queue-edge-cutover-and-kernel-slice-hints-for-continuous-batcher
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Continuous batching at high concurrency exhibits worst-case starvation and tail latency spikes for KV-heavy requests when long-lived pinned keys occupy slots. This PR introduces a decoupled queue-edge cutover and kernel slice hinting mechanism to reduce tail latency while preserving throughput. The design separates admission/queueing and execution handoff: a lightweight queue-edge reconciler performs fairness rebalancing and issues timed cutover windows to avoid head-of-line pinning; the execution handoff now accepts kernel slice hints that allow the runtime to schedule shorter preemptible slices for large attention kernels, improving cooperative fairness between KV-heavy and compute-heavy requests. Summary of changes: 1) runtime/batcher: add queue_edge_reconciler with priority buckets, soft-timeout windows, and probe-driven cutover triggers. 2) runtime/scheduler: implement kernel_slice_hints API and slice budget accounting; expose per-model hint profiles used during model-onboarding. 3) runtime/kvcache: improve pin-awareness by exposing key residency metrics and adding a transient pin-decay policy to reduce long tail for pinned keys. 4) telemetry: new metrics queue_edge_delay_seconds, slice_hint_utilization_ratio, kv_pin_decay_count; dashboards updated. 5) tests/benchmarks: microbench harness for mixed KV+compute workload and e2e perf job with 95th/99th tracking. Behavioral guarantees: soft timeouts are conservative by default and can be tuned via batcher_config.slo_steering; starvation monitor will escalate to emergency cutover that temporarily disables coalescing for offending keys. Backwards compatibility: kernel_slice_hints are optional; default hint profiles preserve current behavior. Performance: mixed workload benchmark on p4d-equivalent nodes shows median latency -6% and p99 tail -18% for KV-heavy routes at 80% load; overall throughput unchanged within 1.5%. Rollout plan: staged canary starting with 5% traffic, monitoring new telemetry for 48 hours, then 25% then global; can be reverted by toggling batcher.queue_edge.enabled. Why this is different: instead of solely adjusting admission timers or batch sizes, this change decouples the queuing semantics from execution slices and surfaces hints to kernel selection so the runtime can make informed preemption decisions, reducing harmful coupling between KV pin duration and large attention kernel runs.
commits: 6 commits: feat(batcher): add queue_edge_reconciler and tests; perf(scheduler): kernel slice hints and budget accounting; feat(kvcache): pin-residency metrics and pin-decay policy; docs: add batcher config and runbook; ci: add mixed-workload benchmark job; fix(tests): flake/timeout adjustments
review_discussion: Initial review requested changes around the default soft-timeout (Arjun asked to make default more conservative) and to add a telemetry counter for emergency cutovers (Sofia). I updated batcher/config.go to expose slo_steering.max_soft_timeout_ms and added queue_edge_emergency_cutovers_total metric. Liam suggested making kernel_slice_hints opt-in via model metadata which I implemented by checking model_profile.slice_hintable flag; this avoided changing default kernels for existing models. CI initially failed on the perf job due to an environment race; I fixed a test harness race by introducing deterministic seeds and re-ran CI; all checks passed. Reviewers approved after the fixes; approvals: Arjun (approve), Sofia (approve), Liam (approve). Author notes: included benchmark harness and runbook for ops to tune soft timeouts during canary.
merge_outcome: merged via squash with commit message 'decoupled queue edge cutover and kernel slice hints for continuous batcher; includes telemetry and runbook'. Merge method: squash+merge. No post-merge conflicts.
release_notes: Adds queue-edge reconciler and kernel slice hinting to reduce p99 for mixed KV+compute workloads; new telemetry (queue_edge_delay_seconds, slice_hint_utilization_ratio, kv_pin_decay_count); config knobs: batcher.queue_edge.enabled, batcher.slo_steering.max_soft_timeout_ms, model_profile.slice_hintable; rollout via canary; no behavior change unless enabled.
